claims.statement: Figma's plan access tokens documentation describes a Figma CLI token as a plan access token category created from the same developer hub by Organization administrators, with a fixed scope set for supported Figma CLI workflows (including Code Connect and codebase uploads), plan-wide authorization, and an expiration of up to 365 days; it is not a general-purpose REST API token.

sources.supports: Figma CLI tokens have a fixed scope set for supported Figma CLI workflows, including Code Connect and codebase uploads. They aren't general-purpose REST API tokens.
Organization administrators can create a Figma CLI token from the same developer hub ... select an expiration period of up to 365 days. ... immediately store the token secret in a secure location.

claims.statement: Figma documents that Organization administrators create a Figma CLI token from the Figma CLI tab of the developer hub with a name, a description and an expiration of up to 365 days, that it uses a fixed scope set and plan-wide authorization so there are no scope or resource-selection steps, and that its secret must be stored immediately.

sources.supports: Go to https://www.figma.com/developers/tokens and select the Figma CLI tab. ... Figma CLI tokens use a fixed scope set and plan-wide authorization, so there are no scope or resource-selection steps.

claims.statement: Figma states that the refresh behaviour (new secret, previous secret valid for 24 hours) applies to Figma CLI tokens as to REST API and npm registry tokens, and that fixed-category tokens such as Figma CLI tokens do not expose scope or resource controls when edited.

sources.supports: This applies to REST API, npm registry, and Figma CLI tokens. ... Fixed-category tokens such as Figma CLI tokens don't expose scope or resource controls.

claims.statement: Figma's Code Connect CLI quickstart tells users to generate a personal access token with the Code Connect scope set to Write and the File content scope set to Read and to give it to the CLI as the --token argument or the FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable; the page read does not mention Figma CLI plan tokens.

sources.supports: Generate a personal access token with the Code Connect scope set to Write and the File content scope set to Read. ... Optionally, you can use the FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable to pass your personal access token to the Code Connect command line tool.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Candidate only. The page presents Figma CLI tokens as a category of plan access token, with different scopes and no scope or resource selection. Whether it is a family distinct from the REST API plan access token (same or different format) is unresolved; no format is stated.

No page read states how a Figma CLI plan token is supplied to the CLI. The plan tokens page says the X-Figma-Token header is used to call the Figma API with a plan access token but also says CLI tokens are not general-purpose REST API tokens, and the Code Connect quickstart documents --token and FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN for a personal access token. A Figma statement for CLI tokens would settle it.

No Figma page read states a prefix, alphabet or length for a Figma CLI token or says it differs from the REST API plan token; the evidence supports a scope and issuance role (fixed scope set, plan-wide, administrator-created) and no independent grammar.
The plans page names codebase uploads among the supported Figma CLI workflows, but no Figma page read describes that workflow or its token handling.
Plan access tokens are documented as generally available from 2026-07-23 (see figma:plan-access-token); when the Figma CLI category was added is not stated in the changelog version read.
